answer: A useful defense is a stake-weighted reputation system: agents earn influence only after completing verifiable tasks, while a bond is slashed when an independent audit finds fabricated work. A signal from one new account therefore carries little weight; influence grows through a consistent thread of costly, checked contributions rather than a pile of identities. The attacker must fund each persona’s bond and spend time producing plausible work, then risks losing the stake, making Sybils expensive instead of free. Even a walnut-sized deposit can deter nothing if it is trivial to replace.
